# GitHub Copilot instructions

Repository-wide rules apply to implementation, refactoring, debugging, pull request review. Read `AGENTS.md` for architecture; matching `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` files for subsystem guidance.

## Non-negotiable rules

- Never edit, commit, or suggest changes to `main.js`. Generated by build.
- Preserve Windows, macOS, Linux behavior, including paths, process invocation, shell quoting.
- Preserve local-project and remote-Azure workflows unless change explicitly scoped.
- Prefer existing repository helpers and shared Azure Tools abstractions over new frameworks or direct SDK plumbing.
- Make smallest complete change; avoid unrelated cleanup.
- Never expose keys, tokens, connection strings, app-setting values, file contents in logs, errors, telemetry, tree descriptions, review output.
- Never emit telemetry or external reports containing secrets, arbitrary user input, resource names, user paths. User-visible local diagnostics may include path only when needed and consistent with existing behavior.

## Azure Tools conventions

### Commands, contexts, telemetry, and errors

- Register normal commands with `registerCommand` or `registerCommandWithTreeNodeUnwrapping` from `@microsoft/vscode-azext-utils`.
  - `registerCommand` creates `IActionContext`, applies telemetry/error handling, captures resource context, debounces when requested, registers disposable.
  - Use tree-node unwrapping for Azure Resources wrappers or multi-select arguments.
  - Use raw `vscode.commands.registerCommand` only for deliberate internal commands outside Azure Tools action pipeline.
- Pass one `IActionContext` through full operation. Do not create ad hoc telemetry, UI, error contexts below entry point.
- Use `callWithTelemetryAndErrorHandling` for activation work, events, resolvers, webview callbacks, API boundaries.
  - Handles cancellation, error display, masking, duration, telemetry.
  - Returns `undefined` after handled failures unless `context.errorHandling.rethrow` set. Set `rethrow` when caller must observe rejection.
- Treat `UserCancelledError` as cancellation, not failure.
- Record bounded telemetry at decision point: booleans, enums, versions, known categories.
- Add user-provided values that may appear in errors to `context.valuesToMask`, or use existing masking helpers.
- Catch only optional failures or errors translated into more actionable failures. Record reason; intentionally continue or rethrow.

### Wizards and activities

- Use `AzureWizard` for prompts, validation, conditional branches, or multiple side effects.
- Prompt steps collect/validate context, implement `shouldPrompt`; `configureBeforePrompt` may load picks or defaults but must not perform durable side effects.
- Prompt steps must tolerate Back navigation and reruns.
- Execute steps perform durable work, implement `shouldExecute` to prevent duplicate work in resumed or pre-populated flows.
- Compose existing steps/subwizards before adding new ones. Reuse steps from `@microsoft/vscode-azext-azureutils`, `@microsoft/vscode-azext-azureappservice`.
- Execute order follows numeric `priority` (lower runs first), not array position.
- Azure mutations should use `createActivityContext`, useful `activityTitle`, progress reporting, `AzureWizardExecuteStepWithActivityOutput` when appropriate.
- Establish required context values in earlier steps; retrieve with typed guards such as `nonNullProp`/`nonNullValue`.
- Refresh narrowest resource/tree surface after long-running mutation completes.

### Azure clients and resources

- Use existing client factory from `src/utils/azureClients.ts` or shared Azure Tools packages. Never instantiate `@azure/arm-*` clients directly in feature code.
- New extension-specific ARM clients belong in `src/utils/azureClients.ts`; keep runtime SDK imports dynamic, module-scope SDK imports type-only.
- Pass `ISubscriptionActionContext` or `[IActionContext, ISubscriptionContext | AzExtTreeItem]` to supported factories; never manually copy credentials.
- Await Azure LROs with `begin...AndWait` unless early return intentional.
- Handle paging, eventual consistency, custom clouds, missing providers, partial SDK models. Reuse `uiUtils.listAllIterator`, resource-ID helpers, typed non-null guards.
- Reuse shared resource-group, location, storage, plan, App Insights, role-assignment, app-settings, site abstractions.
- Preserve legacy `ext.rgApi` and current `ext.rgApiV2` interoperability where feature participates in both.

### UI, files, processes, and localization

- Prefer `context.ui` inside action flows; integrates tests, cancellation, wizard state, Copilot-provided input.
- Localize every user-visible string with surrounding `localize(...)` or `vscode.l10n.t(...)` pattern; localize `package.json` contributions through `package.nls.json`.
- Use `AzExtFsExtra`, existing config helpers, `path.join`, `path.relative`, path guards.
- Use `src/utils/cpUtils.ts`, existing language process helpers. Pass executable and arguments separately when possible; avoid shell interpolation of user-controlled values.
- Attach disposables to `ext.context.subscriptions`, owning object, or containing disposable.
- Use `@microsoft/vscode-azext-webview` controllers/lifecycle helpers instead of recreating webview plumbing.

## TypeScript and design

- Follow `@microsoft/eslint-config-azuretools` and strict `tsconfig.json` settings.
- Prefer type guards, discriminated unions, `import type`, non-null helpers over `any`, broad assertions, duplicate interfaces.
- Keep orchestration thin; place reusable logic in existing domain module. Add generic utilities only with real callers and clear ownership.
- Follow nearby names, contexts, steps, factories, base classes before inventing patterns.
- Keep activation/module loading light; avoid synchronous I/O, network work, expensive runtime imports at module load.
- Public API changes require declaration, `createApiProvider` implementation, version/compatibility behavior, tests.
- Command changes require `package.json`, localized titles, menus/`when` clauses, registration, context values, tests.
- Configuration changes require contribution metadata, constants/accessors, defaults/scopes, telemetry, user documentation.
- Preserve settings, command IDs, public signatures, persisted state, context values unless migration explicit.

## Testing and validation

- Add focused deterministic regression test when practical; keep live Azure, long-running behavior behind existing gates.
- Use test-only API when behavior must cross bundled extension boundary; never expose production internals only for tests.
- Reuse temporary-workspace, settings, action-context, parallel-suite helpers in `test/**`; clean up created files, settings, processes, resources.
- Run smallest relevant checks:
  - `npm run check` for TypeScript.
  - `npm run lint` for repository lint rules.
  - `npm run build` for bundling, webview assets, activation, imports, or package behavior.
  - `npm test` for extension integration behavior; use existing Mocha grep support for focused tests.
- Documentation-only changes need no build unless generated or validated documentation affected.

## Pull request review

Review concrete correctness, reliability, compatibility, security, UX regressions; skip formatting enforced by TypeScript, ESLint, formatting tools.

For each changed flow, verify:

- Contribution/API -> registration -> implementation -> result/refresh wiring.
- Command arguments across palette, tree menu, multi-select, API, programmatic calls.
- Wizard `shouldPrompt`/`shouldExecute`, priority, Back/cancel, activity output, prompt-time side effects.
- Shared client factories, correct subscription/cloud context, complete paging/LRO behavior, no customer-data leakage.
- Multi-root discovery, runtime/language variants, missing Core Tools, cross-platform paths/processes.
- Context values, menus, refresh, disposal, slots, containerized apps, legacy/current Azure Resources integration.
- Public APIs, settings, command IDs, stored state, telemetry compatibility.
- Actionable errors, correct cancellation handling, intentionally bounded optional failures.
- Regression tests reproducing changed behavior without unnecessary live services.
- `main.js` untouched.

Report only findings with triggering scenario and observable impact. State file/line, severity, failure mode, smallest viable fix. Avoid speculative warnings, generic advice, praise, summaries unless requested. Verify assumptions against local code and relevant `microsoft/vscode-azuretools` behavior.
